title.narrative: UNFPA support to Country Programme South Sudan 2023-2025

description.narrative:
The overall vision of the UNFPA Country Programme 2023-2025 is that every woman, girl and youth in South Sudan is empowered and enjoys quality sexual and reproductive health and rights and gender equality; and gender-based violence, including child marriage, is reduced. The outputs are identified as follows:
Output 1: Women, youth and marginalized populations have increased access to equitable and people-centred maternal health, family planning, gender-based violence and HIV prevention information and services through a strengthened and robust health system.*
Output 2: Strengthened capacities of actors, institutions, and mechanisms to address discriminatory gender and social norms and to advance gender equality and women and girls agency, across the humanitarian, development and peace continuum.
Output 3: Strengthened data systems and evidence, especially those related to sexual and reproductive health and rights, gender-based violence and population changes.
Output 4: Strengthened capacity of actors and systems to provide timely, peace-responsive, conflict and climate-sensitive life-saving interventions to crisis-affected populations.
Output 5: Youth and adolescents, especially young women facing multiple forms of discrimination, are empowered to demand and access their rights to sexual and reproductive health and reject gender-based violence and harmful practices, across the humanitarian, development and peace continuum.

Landprogrammets övergripande vision är att varje kvinna, flicka och ungdom i Sydsudan ska kunna åtnjuta sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter av hög kvalitet, att jämställdhet mellan kvinnor och män ökar och att könsrelaterat våld, inklusive barnäktenskap, minskar. Arbetet kommer att genomföras med särskilt fokus på att stärka hälsosystemet i landet, adressera diskriminerande och hälsoskadande normer, främja jämställdhet, bistå med livsavgörande insatser till människor i kris med särskilt fokus på förebyggande och behandlande insatser relaterat till könsrelaterat våld samt främja sexuella och reproduktiva rättigheter. Implementering sker i stor utsträckning med hjälp av både internationella och nationella civilsamhälles organisationer.

The overall vision of the country programme is that every woman, girl and youth in South Sudan is empowered and enjoys quality sexual and reproductive health and rights and gender equality; and gender based violence, including child marriage, is reduced. The work will be carried out with a specific focus on strengthening the health system in the country, addressing discriminatory and health-damaging norms, promoting gender equality, assisting with life-changing interventions for people in crisis with a particular focus on preventive and treatment interventions related to gender-related violence and promoting sexual and reproductive rights. Implementation of programme activities will to a large extent be arranged with the help of both international and national non-governmental organizations.

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

description.narrative:
Output level reporting 2024
The Country Programme focuses on five key result areas aimed at accelerating the reduction of unmet need for family planning, reduction of preventable maternal deaths, and reduction of GBV with harmful practices, including child marriage.
Output 1: By 2025, women, youth and marginalised populations have increased access to equitable and people-centred maternal health, family planning, gender-based violence and HIV prevention information and services through a strengthened and robust health system.
All output indicators for 2024 were achieved. Some key results include:
- The number of women using Family Planning increased by 90% (i.e., an increase from 100 000 in 2023 to 190 000).
- A total of 200 811 adolescents and young people accessed SRH services through both standalone and integrated AYSRH services and health facilities across the country.
- A total of 891 153 people, mainly women and girls, were provided with SRH services at 22 targeted health facilities.
- Male engagement strategy implemented to enhance male participation in FP/SRH/GBV programs was developed.
Output 2: By 2025, strengthened capacities of actors, institutions, and mechanisms to address discriminatory gender and social norms to advance gender equality and women and girls agency across humanitarian, development, and peace continuum.
All output indicators for 2024 were achieved. Some key results include:
- 16 822 individuals (4 143 men and boys, 12 679 women and girls) reached with massages on gender equality, social norms, GBV, and ending child marriage and early pregnancy during community mobilisation and sensitisation.
- 10 432 vulnerable groups members (persons with disability, persons living with HIV) reached with messages on human rights commitments and recommendations related to gender equality and discrimination.
- Through the national campaign, more than 10 005 community members were reached and 118 school and university students engaged in positive masculinity discussions and awareness raising.
Output 3: By 2025, strengthened data systems and evidence, especially those related to sexual and reproductive health and rights, gender-based violence and population changes.
Four out of five indicators for 2024 were achieved. Some key results include:
- 224 key staff from the National Bureau of statistics and other government data gathering agencies were trained in data collection and analysis methodologies.
- 250 national and state level planners were trained on integration of population issues in planning and budgetary frameworks.
- 98 staff from Ministries of Health and Gender were trained on how to generate, analyse, produce, and disseminate SRH/GBV data.
The indicator ''functional real-time central management information system on GBV established'' was reported as only partially achieved. Although the real-time central management information system on GBV was developed and tested for Ministry of Gender, Child, and Social Welfare, its full roll out has been hindered by insufficient government counterpart funding.
Output 4: By 2025, strengthened capacity of actors and systems strengthened to provide timely, peace-responsive, conflict and climate-sensitive, life-saving interventions to crisis-affected populations.
Four out of five indicators for 2024 were achieved. Some key results:
- For 2023 and 2024, 535 822 individuals were reached with integrated lifesaving GBV/SRH Services.
- Training was provided to 1 077 service providers on MISP and different components.
- A database for service providers trained on MISP across the country.
- UNFPA supported community-based complaint mechanism networks that support raising awareness on PSEA within the community. These community-based mechanisms have successfully contributed to promoting GBV prevention and response services within the community.
The indicator ''number of service providers trained to provide Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) and other conflict and climate-sensitive interventions'' fell slightly short of the target, reaching 1 478 out of 1 500. However, Sida does not consider this a concern due to the small margin of difference.
Output 5: By 2025, youth and adolescents, especially young women facing multiple forms of discrimination are empowered to demand and access their rights to sexual and reproductive health and reject gender-based violence and harmful practices across the humanitarian, development, and peace continuum.
All output indicators for 2024 were achieved. Some key results include:
- A total of 138 000 young people were reached with Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE) information.
- 18 institutions were equipped with staff trained in the operationalisation of out-of-school CSE for young people.
- A youth-led digital solution was successfully launched, providing young people with crucial information and services on SRHR, Family Planning, HIV&AIDS Gender Equality, and GBV.
The outputs are generally regarded as successful, except for two indicators in output 3 and 4. As mentioned earlier, one indicator fell slightly short of its target, while the other had a valid reason for not meeting its goal. Additionally, Sida noted that most indicators across the five logframe outputs were met, often exceeding their targets. Sida considers the explanations provided for the unmet targets to be reasonable and satisfactory.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
